subject: Edge routing & KMS latency: SLA responsibility clarification request
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skybridge-labs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@skybridge-labs.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification request: routing & KMS latency allocation for private VPC

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Dedicated + Private flow looks promising. As we lock down procurement, our security team asked for a short note on how Redwood will treat latency impacts that originate from customer-managed edge routers and our KMS (we host an external HSM in our VPC).

Specifically:
- If our edge router (customer-managed) drops or delays packets, how will that be attributed against the SLA?
- If an egress-heavy key unwrap operation from our KMS adds 50–200ms occasionally, can that be scoped out of Redwood's latency SLO?

We have a short diagram and a proposed addendum (attached) that shows the handoff point where we think the responsibility should flip to Skybridge. Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign an appendix that explicitly excludes these customer-controlled elements from latency calculations, and what evidence you would need to support that exclusion?

I attached the addendum and an edge routing diagram for reference. Procurement may loop in a PO/DocuSign step after legal signs off.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — we’re trying to close the contract by EOW.

Best,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Cloud Platform, Skybridge Labs

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification request: routing & KMS latency allocation for private VPC

Alex —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the diagrams. Short answer: we can accept an appendix that excludes customer-controlled network and customer-managed KMS operations from Redwood's latency SLO, but we need a narrow, testable definition and an evidence protocol.

High-level requirements we would need to include in the appendix:
1) Handoff point: a single IP/CIDR or NAT/gateway hostname where Redwood’s telemetry considers the request in. We’ll exclude latency upstream of that hop.
2) Evidence: packet capture (pcap) or equivalent logs for representative incidents, and KMS request/response timestamps showing the added latency window.
3) Operational guardrails: when the excluded element is causing >5% of token latency across a 24h window, we reserve the right to trigger a mitigation plan (traffic-shifting or temporary routing change).
4) Monitoring hooks: a shared health endpoint and a lightweight heartbeat file (simple 200 OK) that the customer exposes so our routing can validate reachability.

Irene and Karthik — can you weigh in on whether the handoff-definition above is sufficient from infra/legal POV? I think the evidence list can be pared down to logs + sample pcaps for most customers, but open to suggestions.

If that’s acceptable to you Alex, I can draft the appendix language and circulate for signature.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Naomi / Irene / Alex —

Couple of legal/operational notes from my side:
- We should avoid blanket exclusions that would make the SLA meaningless. Draft language should say: "Latency attributed to customer-controlled components (as defined by the handoff IP/hostname and corroborating logs) will be excluded from Redwood's latency calculations provided the customer submits evidence within 5 business days of an incident."
- Evidence scope: (i) application timestamp traces showing request ingress and egress, (ii) KMS operation logs with request ids and durations, (iii) network path summary (traceroute) for the period the incident occurred. We can accept pcap for high-severity incidents only.
- KMS caveat: if the customer uses a KMS configuration that causes repeated high tail latency (more than 2% of requests in a month), we need an operational plan requiring the customer to optimize or move keys to a supported managed KMS profile; otherwise we reserve rights to count those events against the SLA after repeated occurrences.

Irene — can infra confirm that a single handoff hostname + traceroute + KMS logs will be sufficient to programmatically exclude samples from our analytics pipeline? If not, list the fields we need to request from the customer.

I will draft proposed clause language and circulate a redline by EOD.

—Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skybridge-labs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 May 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification request: routing & KMS latency allocation for private VPC

Thanks Naomi / Karthik — that approach sounds reasonable and conservative. Procurement attached our revised addendum with slightly tightened evidence timelines (we can provide traceroutes and KMS request ids within 48 hours for incidents) — see attached.

We’re good to proceed with a short appendix that references:
- Handoff: public-ip:203.0.113.22 (Skybridge NAT gateway)
- Evidence: application traces, traceroute, KMS request ids (48-hour turnaround for initial incidents)
- Pilot period: first 90 days we treat these exclusions as "informational" (they won’t count against Redwood's SLO but will be used to tune the routing). After 90 days, they become binding per clause.

Can you send the DocuSign when legal is ready? If it helps, procurement will sign on receipt of the redline + final appendix PDF.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
Procurement CC: procurement@skybridge-labs.com
